units.translation: Philoxenus in Etym. M. p.31, 5 believed that it was said for αρχαιότατον [most ancient], because ἀρχαιέστατος [most ancient] should have been said, as αἰδοιέστατος [most revered], which he himself compares, is said. The word, abnormal in form and unsuitable to the sense, Lobeck wished to change to ἀρχέστρατος [leader of the host] in Paralip. p. 81 and Pathol. Elem. vol. 1 p. 337, who conjectured that these were the words of Ulysses conversing with Penelope, to whom, when he first came into her sight, he lied that he was a prince of Crete, Odyss. 19, 180. L. Dindorf in Thes. vol. 1, 2 p. 2107 conjectured that a proper name different from Αἴθων [Aethon], which Homer has, lies hidden. Nauck in de Aristoph. Byzantio p. 46 thinks it is the superlative of the substantive ἀρχός [leader], which however should rather be written ἀρχίστατος [nearest] and perhaps is to be restored at Ag. 256 for ἄγχιστον [nearest]. See ἄγχιστος.

The same ἀπ᾿ ἀρχῆς [from the beginning] appears in a corrupt passage written thus in M

where the scholium has: the sequence, "it is fitting and owed to me to praise the first-fruits (i.e. ἀπ᾿ ἀρχᾶς [from the beginning]) of life of those who carry me by force," etc. and similarly in another scholium: "it is fitting and owed to me, since I have taken up this life (here too it reads ἀπ' ἀρχᾶς βίου [from the beginning of life]) to praise the possessions of those who have acquired them by force." Most apt is what Schuetz conjectured: πρέπον τύχαις βίου [fitting to the fortunes of life], except that he should rather have written τύχας [fortunes], as Heimsoeth did, joining the words δίκαια καὶ — βίου [just and — of life] into one verse, with the last syllable of δίκαια [just] lengthened.
under no one's rule.
